public_rationale: Marcus said even o1 shows accuracy falling off as multiplication problems get bigger. In September 2024, Yuntian Deng tested o1 on problems up to 20x20 digits. He reported that o1 'solves up to 9x9 multiplication with decent accuracy.' That implies its accuracy drops beyond that size. TechCrunch reported Deng's finding that o1 got 9x9 problems right only about half the time. Both sources also say o1 did much better than GPT-4o, which fits 'even o1': o1 improved but still showed the same fall-off. A 2025 study found o1 got every 5x5 problem right, which is consistent with a decline that starts only at larger sizes.
limitations: The evidence comes from a researcher's post and a news report, not a peer-reviewed paper.
The model tested in Sept 2024 was o1-preview or o1-mini, not the later full o1.

our_interpretation: Read as: at the time of the post, evaluations of OpenAI's o1 (the o1-preview/o1-mini models available in Sept-Oct 2024) showed its multiplication accuracy dropping as operands got longer.
No threshold is given; any clear decline from high accuracy on small problems to low accuracy on larger ones counts.
criteria.support_condition: An evaluation of o1 by operand size shows accuracy falling as the number of digits rises.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An evaluation shows o1 keeping high accuracy across all operand sizes tested (for example up to 20x20).
